title: Concilium Romanum I (AD 0494)
author: Gelasius I
source: Translated by Claude from tmp946.tmp946.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: Item Vitas Patrum, Pauli, Antonii, Hilarionis, et omnium eremitarum quas tamen vir beatissimus scripsit Hieronymus, cum omni honore suscipimus.
passages.english: Likewise the Lives of the Fathers, of Paul, of Antony, of Hilarion, and of all the hermits, which, however, that most blessed man Jerome wrote, we receive with all honour.
passages.notes: The 'tamen' ('however') is awkward in the sentence. Other versions of this decree read 'quas tamen vir beatissimus scripsit Hieronymus' in the same way.

passages.original: Item chronica Eusebii Cæsariensis, et ejusdem ecclesiasticæ Historiae libros : quamvis in primo narrationis suae libro lepuerit, et postea in laudibus atque excusatione Origenis schismatici unum con- I scripserit librum : propter rerum tamen notitiam singularem, quæ ad instructionem pertinent, usquequaque non dicimus renuendos. r Item Orosium virum eruditissimum colJaudamus : quia valde nobis necessariam adversus paganorum calumnias dignam ordinavit historiam miraque brevitale contexuit.
passages.english: Likewise the chronicle of Eusebius of Caesarea and the books of his Ecclesiastical History: although in the first book of his narrative he grew lukewarm, and afterwards wrote one book in praise and defence of Origen the schismatic, nevertheless, on account of his singular knowledge of things that pertain to instruction, we do not say that they are to be rejected altogether. Likewise we praise Orosius, a most learned man, because he composed for us a worthy history, very necessary against the calumnies of the pagans, and wove it together with wonderful brevity.
passages.notes: 'lepuerit' is a scanning error, apparently for 'tepuerit' ('grew lukewarm'). Some versions of this text read 'tacuerit' ('was silent'), but that reading is not attested here. Several other scanning errors have been silently corrected: 'con- I scripserit' (conscripserit), the stray 'r', 'colJaudamus' (collaudamus) and 'brevitale' (brevitate). 'Usquequaque non dicimus renuendos' is rendered 'we do not say ... to be rejected altogether'. It could also be read as 'we say they are by no means to be rejected'.
